Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testMath274` expects that the constructor of `CholeskyDecompositionImpl` throws a `NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException` when given a matrix that is not symmetric positive definite. The test provides a 4x4 matrix which is supposed to be symmetric positive definite, but the test fails because the exception is not thrown.

Inspecting the code of `CholeskyDecompositionImpl.CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix, double, double)`, the constructor first checks that the matrix is square (which it is). Then it assigns the matrix data to a local variable `lTData`.

Then the constructor performs a validation loop over the matrix:
- It checks if each diagonal element is greater than or equal to an absolute positivity threshold (line 114). If any diagonal element is less than this threshold, it throws `NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException`.
- For each pair of off-diagonal elements `(i,j)` and `(j,i)`, it compares their difference with a threshold based on a relative symmetry threshold times the larger absolute value of the two. If the difference exceeds this threshold, it throws `NotSymmetricMatrixException`. After this check, it resets the element at `(j,i)` to zero.

After these validations, it proceeds to perform the Cholesky transformation.

The key insight is in line 114 where the diagonal elements are checked against `absolutePositivityThreshold`. If any diagonal element has a value less than this threshold, the exception is thrown immediately.

The test matrix has some diagonal elements close to zero but positive. The test expects an exception because it is not positive definite, but the constructor might not be detecting this correctly due to the combination of the absolute positivity threshold and how the test matrix is constructed.

Also, the input matrix in the test has a negative off-diagonal element `-0.09376327` (line 84), but the code checks symmetry allowing some threshold difference. The code checks if `abs(lIJ - lJI)` <= `maxDelta` and resets `lJ[i]` to zero otherwise it throws.

From the bug report and test, the user expects that the matrix is symmetric positive definite, but with a negative element it might not be symmetric positive definite strictly. This suggests the constructor might be too lenient or the thresholds might be too tolerant, so it does not throw the expected exception for non-positive definite matrices.

In summary, the bug occurs because the `CholeskyDecompositionImpl` constructor does not correctly identify the input matrix as not positive definite (hence does not throw `NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException` as the test expects). This could be because of the threshold constants used in the constructor allowing matrices that are not strictly symmetric positive definite to pass.

Recent bug reports are unrelated and do not contribute to this diagnosis. The root cause lies in the threshold checks in the constructor validation logic in `CholeskyDecompositionImpl.CholeskyDecompositionImpl(org.apache.commons.math.linear.RealMatrix, double, double)`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
